posts.html:
Our lead reporter brings you live, on-the-ground updates straight from the press room as officials unveil the latest policy changes and community initiatives. Procedural votes this week will show whether the coalition holds.

Aides said the timetable could still slip if amendments multiply on the floor. Lawmakers from both parties described the moment as fragile but workable.

People familiar with the discussions, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to comment publicly, said the outcome had been in doubt until late in the process. The White House declined to comment on the details before a formal briefing.

Why it matters

The decision touches millions of people directly and many more indirectly. Supporters call it overdue; critics say it moves too fast and explains too little. Both camps agree the next six months will show whether it works.

What happens next

The White House declined to comment on the details before a formal briefing. Our reporters will follow the story as it develops.

It is the most consequential decision of the year, and it was made quietly.

Reporting was contributed by the Politics desk. This article has been updated with additional detail.

posts.html:
The Gulf Coast flood season has arrived six weeks early as shifting atmospheric patterns bring repeated heavy rain. Temperatures will fall sharply behind the front.

Emergency managers urged residents to check local alerts. The models agreed unusually early on the storm’s track.

People familiar with the discussions, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to comment publicly, said the outcome had been in doubt until late in the process. Forecasters expect the pattern to persist into next week.

Why it matters

The decision touches millions of people directly and many more indirectly. Supporters call it overdue; critics say it moves too fast and explains too little. Both camps agree the next six months will show whether it works.

What happens next

Forecasters expect the pattern to persist into next week. Our reporters will follow the story as it develops.

It is the most consequential decision of the year, and it was made quietly.

Reporting was contributed by the Weather desk. This article has been updated with additional detail.

Analysts expect neighbouring governments to respond cautiously. Diplomats in both capitals described the agreement as overdue.

People familiar with the discussions, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to comment publicly, said the outcome had been in doubt until late in the process. Officials said implementation would begin within ninety days.

Why it matters

The decision touches millions of people directly and many more indirectly. Supporters call it overdue; critics say it moves too fast and explains too little. Both camps agree the next six months will show whether it works.

What happens next

Officials said implementation would begin within ninety days. Our reporters will follow the story as it develops.

It is the most consequential decision of the year, and it was made quietly.

The decision touches millions of people directly and many more indirectly. Supporters call it overdue; critics say it moves too fast and explains too little. Both camps agree the next six months will show whether it works.

Traders said volumes were well above the thirty-day average. Our reporters will follow the story as it develops.

Negotiators reached a tentative agreement hours before the deadline. The White House declined to comment on the details before a formal briefing.

Procedural votes this week will show whether the coalition holds. Lawmakers from both parties described the moment as fragile but workable.

People familiar with the discussions, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to comment publicly, said the outcome had been in doubt until late in the process. Aides said the timetable could still slip if amendments multiply on the floor.

Why it matters

The decision touches millions of people directly and many more indirectly. Supporters call it overdue; critics say it moves too fast and explains too little. Both camps agree the next six months will show whether it works.

What happens next

Aides said the timetable could still slip if amendments multiply on the floor. Our reporters will follow the story as it develops.

It is the most consequential decision of the year, and it was made quietly.

Reporting was contributed by the U.S desk. This article has been updated with additional detail.
